author: Cameron Drummond
title: Keeneland reports the first horse death of the track's 2026 Spring Meet - NewsBreak
text:
By Cameron Drummond ,
5 hours ago On Wednesday, Keeneland reported the first horse death from a racing incident at the 2026 Spring Meet. Tasha Poullard/tpoullard@herald-leader.com A horse died Wednesday at Keeneland following a racing incident during the third day of the track’s 2026 Spring Meet in Lexington.
During the eighth and final race of Wednesday’s card, a racing incident on the backstretch of Keeneland’s main dirt track led to the death of 3-year-old High Go.
According to the Equibase race chart , High Go bumped against another horse while passing the five-furlong pole and fell during the seven-furlong starter allowance race with a purse of $63,000. The racing surface was listed as fast.
High Go was transported from the track in an equine ambulance. According to Keeneland’s safety report , High Go sustained a fractured right shoulder before being administered humane euthanasia.
“High Go was attended to by an expert team of veterinarians led by KHGRC Chief Veterinarian Dr. Nick Smith, in consultation with Keeneland Vice President of Equine Safety Dr. Stuart Brown,” the safety report read. “... We express our sincere condolences to High Go’s connections, owner Calumet Farm and trainer Brendan Walsh.”
High Go’s 31-year-old jockey, Tyler Gaffalione, was able to walk away from the incident. He was evaluated by UK HealthCare medical staff and cleared.
High Go was taking part in its sixth career race, and its first at Keeneland. The Calumet Farm homebred began its racing career in September at Churchill Downs in Louisville. High Go then raced at Horseshoe Indianapolis in October in Indiana, followed by three races in November, January and March at Fair Grounds in New Orleans.
High Go’s lone victory came in a maiden optional claiming race at Fair Grounds on New Year’s Day. High Go was trained by Brendan Walsh and owned by Calumet Farm. The horse’s sire was Hightail and the mare was Southern Dynamo, who was by Dynaformer.
High Go is the first horse to die following a racing incident at Keeneland during the 2026 Spring Meet, which began Friday.
Last year, at least five horses died at Keeneland following racing incidents across the Spring and Fall Meets.
